titleEn: Garage Renovation Cost Vancouver 2026 — Complete Guide
contentEn:
How much does a garage renovation cost in Vancouver? This guide covers everything from foundation to drywall, permits, and timelines. Reno Stars has been transforming homes across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and the broader Metro Vancouver area for over 15 years. This guide covers the key renovation categories, average costs, and what homeowners should know before signing a contract.

What Is the Average Cost of a Full-Home Renovation in Vancouver?

A full-home renovation in Vancouver typically ranges from $150 to $400 per square foot, depending on scope. A complete renovation of a 2,000 sq ft home can cost anywhere from $300,000 to $800,000 or more when structural work, plumbing, and electrical are involved. Minor renovations — such as updating finishes, repainting, and replacing fixtures — can start around $30,000 to $75,000 for a single room.

Costs vary significantly by city. Renovation costs in Richmond tend to run 10–15% higher than in outlying areas like Surrey or Langley, primarily due to permit fees and labor availability. Burnaby and North Vancouver fall in the middle range.

Do You Need a Permit for a Vancouver Home Renovation?

Most structural renovations in Vancouver proper require a building permit from the City of Vancouver. This includes any work that alters load-bearing walls, adds square footage, or modifies plumbing and electrical systems. Cosmetic work — painting, flooring replacement, and fixture swaps — generally does not require a permit.

In Metro Vancouver municipalities, permit requirements vary: Richmond requires permits for any structural change, while Surrey has a simplified process for smaller additions. Always check with your local building department before starting.

How Long Does a Whole-Home Renovation Take?

A whole-home renovation in Vancouver typically takes 4 to 12 months, depending on scope. Cosmetic-only renovations may be completed in 4–8 weeks. A major renovation involving structural changes, new bathrooms, and a kitchen remodel can take 6–12 months. Heritage homes may require additional time for compliance reviews.

What Is the Most Expensive Room to Renovate in a Vancouver Home?

Kitchens and bathrooms are consistently the most expensive rooms to renovate in Vancouver. A full kitchen renovation — including cabinetry, countertops, appliances, and plumbing — can cost $35,000 to $120,000 or more. A primary bathroom renovation similarly ranges from $25,000 to $80,000 depending on finishes and whether layout changes are involved.

How Do I Choose a Renovation Contractor in Vancouver?

When selecting a contractor in Vancouver, look for proper licensing (CRDC in BC), proof of insurance, and a detailed contract that specifies scope, timeline, and payment schedule. Obtain at least three written estimates and ask for references from recent projects in your area. Reno Stars provides free, no-obligation quotes for all renovation projects in Metro Vancouver.

Is 2026 a good year to renovate in Vancouver?

Yes — material costs have stabilized in early 2026 following global supply chain disruptions. Labor availability in Metro Vancouver remains tight, so booking a contractor 4–8 weeks in advance is recommended for most projects.

Does homeowner's insurance cover renovation costs?

Standard homeowner's insurance covers sudden damage (fire, water, storm) but does not cover gradual wear and tear or planned renovations. For major renovations, discuss builder's risk insurance with your contractor.

What is the deposit limit for BC renovation contracts?

BC consumer protection rules limit deposits on renovation contracts to no more than 10% of the total contract value, payable to a licensed contractor. Reno Stars adheres to all BC consumer protection guidelines.
